pagedata.pyUsage:
This activity is used by user interfaces to show the differences between two pages. Use the activity pxComparePagesByKey if you have the pzInsKey of two records to compare.
The extension point pyGetInstanceLabel can be used to customize how the page names are shown on the returned Result page.
Use blacklisting to remove properties from a page structure in bulk. To blacklist create a data transform with an appropriate applies-to class and populate it with the properties or embedded pages to be ignored (property values in the Target column; Source is not needed). Use the applyIgnoreMap method to remove all referenced properties from the page.
The applyIgnoreMap method can be accessed with the following code: tools.getCompareTools().applyIgnoreMap(myPage, "myIgnoreMapName"). The applyIgnoreMap method receives the clipboard page to be updated and the data transform with blacklisted properties or pages (which will be applied recursively to each embedded page).
The reverse, Whitelisting, is also possible. The applyWhiteList method takes the same input parameters but performs the inverse of applyIgnoreMap, keeping only those properties which are referenced in the data transform. White lists are exposed in the pxComparePages and pxComparePagesByKey rule APIs via the WhiteList parameter.

rowdata.pxWarningMessage: Writing application logic using the Java activity method impacts maintainability, discourages reusability, and increases risk during upgrades. Use this method only when necessary. If executing Java code is required, consider using the Call-Function activity method to execute a Function rule. Using Function rules encourages creating well-defined input and output parameters and can be reused across many different types of rules.
The use of activity rules should be limited. The need for activities can be reduced by using data transforms, as well as techniques such as case management, the Engine API, and declaratives.
You should create a test case for this rule to identify any regression issues that might occur when this rule is modified.
